clue.text: Deteriorates, but manages to understand before doctor starts

indicators.note: 'before' places the understanding ahead of the next piece in the answer

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, so 'manages' gives runs
taken as written
to see is to understand, as in 'I see what you mean'

indicators.note: the starts of a word are its opening letters, here just the first letter of doctor

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a problem and gets to grips with it before the doctor arrives, though things are getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that runs to seed has gone past its best, so the phrase is an idiom for declining or going downhill.

clue.text: Minister's time invested in incomplete log

indicators.note: something invested in a thing is placed within it, so the time letter goes inside
an incomplete word has lost its final letter

parts.note: a log is a written record

explanation.surface: A government minister spends time going through an unfinished logbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister's' reads as possessive, but the 's is just 'is' linking the definition to the wordplay. 'incomplete' cuts RECORD to RECOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest in the Church of England, and a clergyman is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Advise on it, possibly fairly heartlessly

indicators.note: 'possibly' suggests the letters of 'on it' could be arranged another way
a word treated heartlessly loses all its inner letters, leaving just its two ends

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give advice on a matter, perhaps fairly but without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns ON IT into NOTI; 'heartlessly' strips fairly down to its outer letters F and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To notify someone is to inform or advise them of something, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Article on green skill and ability to empathise

parts.note: 'the' is the definite article in grammar
a village green is a piece of common land
a deft touch is a skill or knack

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a green space celebrates both talent and fellow feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like a colour or an environmental adjective, but here it is a noun: an open grassy space shared by a village.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with the common touch relates easily to ordinary people, an idiom for being able to understand and share their feelings.

clue.text: Wild cheers engulf mostly boring planner

indicators.note: to engulf something is to swallow it up, so the cheers surround the next piece
wild cheers are disordered, so their letters are rearranged
'mostly' keeps most of a word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: something boring is dull

explanation.surface: An audience's raucous applause drowns out a tedious organiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' gives SCHEER, which 'engulf' splits after SCHE to swallow the trimmed word that 'mostly' leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheduler draws up timetables and arranges when things happen, so a scheduler is a kind of planner.

clue.text: Winter generally sees this bird going west

indicators.note: in an across-style reading, going west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards
the phrase 'Winter generally' sees, or contains, the bird spelt across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: In winter you usually spot this bird flying off westwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' points to TERGE across the join in 'wintER GEnerally'; 'going west' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white wading bird of the heron family.

clue.text: One fashionable old star of the silver screen

definitions.meaning: a person who is fashionable and adored, a celebrity worshipped by fans

definitions.text: old star of the silver screen
definitions.meaning: a heart-throb of old cinema, as in the matinee pin-up of the 1920s and 1930s

explanation.surface: A trendy veteran of the old film industry.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a hero-worshipped celebrity; the matinee version was a classic movie heart-throb.

clue.text: Motor City, America, rejects old rubbish

indicators.note: something that rejects a letter casts it out, so the letter for old is removed

parts.note: Detroit is nicknamed Motor City as the home of the US car industry
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: The car capital of the United States is throwing out its outdated junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' drops the O from DETROITUS, leaving DETRITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter left behind, a synonym for rubbish.

clue.text: Guided around snake, ran

indicators.note: 'around' puts the guiding word around the snake

parts.note: to guide is to lead, so guided gives led
an adder is a venomous snake, the British viper

explanation.surface: Someone steered a path round a snake, then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ran' looks like the verb of fleeing, but it is the sense used of tights or stockings that develop a split run.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights that have laddered have a vertical line of broken stitches, which Americans call a run, so 'ran' fits.

clue.text: Go through my name and split cost of accommodation

parts.note: to pepper a target is to riddle it, going right through with shot
'my!' and 'cor!' are both exclamations of surprise
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Someone tells a flatmate to check their name on the bill and share the housing costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is not possessive but an exclamation, matching the British 'cor!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peppercorn rent is a nominal, very low rent, so it is a token cost for housing.

clue.text: Chop? That is a dish

parts.note: to chop is to cut
i.e. is the abbreviation of the Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A chef points at a cut of meat and asks whether it is a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' sounds culinary given 'Chop', but it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for a good-looking person, so a dish is a cutie.

clue.text: Gathered vets must be worried — hurried around

indicators.note: 'around' sets the hurrying word around the vets' letters

parts.note: to hare is to run fast, so hurried gives hared

indicators.note: worried letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Anxious veterinarians assembled and rushed about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be worried' gives the garment VEST; 'hared' is British informal for running very fast, like a hare.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops that are harvested have been gathered in from the fields.

clue.text: Get rid of rotting cargo

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotting
a load is the cargo carried by a vehicle

explanation.surface: A ship's crew is told to dump goods that have gone bad.
explanation.definitionFit: To offload something is to unload or dispose of it, a synonym for getting rid of it.

clue.text: Joint league leaders?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef from the upper leg, roasted as a Sunday joint
the team at the head of a sports table, read as two words

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about teams who share first place in a league.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as 'shared', but it is a roasting joint of beef; the question mark flags the punning second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean cut of beef for roasting, and the top side is the team leading a league.

clue.text: Little air covering for the earth?

indicators.note: 'covering' puts the air alongside 'for', closing the word off

parts.note: little means small
taken as written
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about the thin layer of air that wraps the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the earth' is the idiom in 'cost the earth', a huge sum; the question mark flags the sly definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironically, a 'small fortune' means a great deal of money, just as something costing the earth is very expensive.

clue.text: Remote possibility to get drunk — fetch a can!

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of order, so the phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at the idea of getting drunk by sending someone for one can of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Fat chance' is an ironic idiom meaning there is very little likelihood of something.

clue.text: Invoice from a poorly expert taking precedence

indicators.note: the expert comes first, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: a pro is a professional or expert

indicators.note: 'poorly' suggests the letters of 'from a' are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bill arrives from an unwell specialist who insists on being seen first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' turns FROM A into FORMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a preliminary invoice sent before goods or services are supplied.

clue.text: Simple and modest without guards, but collapses

indicators.note: the guards of a word are its outer letters standing at each end, so both words lose them

explanation.surface: An unassuming person left unprotected falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that implodes falls inwards on itself, which is a way of collapsing.

clue.text: Earnings of men working with Eurotrain

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and moved about

explanation.surface: A report on what crew members earn from their jobs on a cross-Channel train.
explanation.definitionFit: Remuneration is the pay or salary someone receives, so it is a synonym for earnings.

clue.text: Independent Nationalist covered in blood is cut

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for Independent, as in election results

indicators.note: a letter covered in a word sits inside it

parts.note: gore is spilled blood

explanation.surface: A wounded independent nationalist politician lies bleeding from a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a wound, but it is the verb 'to cut someone', snubbing them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to snub them deliberately, which means to ignore them.

clue.text: Makes slow progress since changes around hotel

indicators.note: 'around' puts the rearranged letters around the hotel letter
'changes' tells you the letters of since are altered in order

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Things have crawled along since the hotel was refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns SINCE into INCES, split to hold H.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to move very slowly, a little at a time.

clue.text: Fellow anticipating full-scale quarrel

indicators.note: to anticipate is to come before, so the fellow letter goes first

parts.note: an all-out effort is a full-scale one

explanation.surface: A man expects an all-out row.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a disagreement between friends, so as a noun it means a quarrel.

clue.text: String quartet's last to get drink

indicators.note: 'last' picks out the final letter of quartet

parts.note: wine is a drink

explanation.surface: The final member of a string quartet goes for a glass of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'String' looks like part of 'String quartet', but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Twine is strong thread or string made of twisted strands.

clue.text: Note to meet international organisation after writing piece

indicators.note: the note and organisation come after the writing

parts.note: a person's hand is their handwriting
G is a musical note
UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A musical note is paired with a body such as the UN after a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang a piece is a firearm, especially a pistol carried by hand.

clue.text: Journalist in fracas gets cut

indicators.note: 'in' places the journalist inside the fracas

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy disturbance or fracas
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter caught up in a brawl gets injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like a wound, but it is a noun meaning a decrease.
explanation.definitionFit: A price cut is a reduction, so the two nouns mean a lowering of amount.

clue.text: Period of lost hope encompassing century

indicators.note: to encompass is to surround, so the century letter goes inside
lost letters have gone astray and been jumbled

parts.note: C is a hundred in Roman numerals, hence century

explanation.surface: A hundred years when hope was gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' turns HOPE into EPOH, split to take C.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a distinct era or period of history.

clue.text: In despair, in retreat, find space for altar

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the hidden letters are read in reverse
'In' says the word lies within despair

explanation.surface: A worshipper in despair withdraws to find room for prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' hides ESPA inside 'dESPAir'; 'in retreat' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the vaulted recess at the east end of a church where the altar usually stands.

clue.text: Soldiers advanced without being persistent

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
to advance money is to lend it, so advanced gives lent
less means without, as in 'pay less tax'

explanation.surface: Troops pushed forward and kept going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' looks like moving forward, but it is money advanced as a loan.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone relentless never gives up, so they are persistent.
